subject: Learning Methods
title: Making Inferences
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Making Inferences.

hook.text: The text said 'the streets were deserted and store shutters were down.' It didn't say 'ghost town' but you thought it.

buildup.text: Inference is reading between the lines: drawing conclusions from clues the author provides without stating them.

discovery.text: Skilled readers make inferences constantly and automatically. Weaker readers take the text only at face value.

twist.text: Over-inference is a risk. Adding too much of your own interpretation can distort the author's intended meaning.

climax.text: Ask 'what does the author imply here?' at key points. Check your inference against the text to avoid projection.

punchline.text: Read what is said. Also read what is implied. Both matter.

quiz.question: What is the risk of over-inference while reading?
options: It slows down reading speed significantly
Adding too much interpretation can distort the author's meaning
It causes you to skip important paragraphs
